ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening, prior to engagement and on a rolling 90-day basis, of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized dealers against: (i) UN Consolidated List, (ii) OFAC SDN List, (iii) Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions (Special Economic Measures Act) and Criminal Code s 83.05 listed entities, (iv) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and (v) BC and federal government PEP references. PEP status follows the FINTRAC definition (PEPs and heads of international organizations, their family members and close associates) with enhanced due diligence applied whenever status is flagged; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documents must be independently corroborated. Screening results and search logic are archived in the AML compliance file for 5 years per PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca) by the Corporate Registry, Office of the Registrar of Companies, BC Ministry of Finance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, s 22 and BC Reg 246/2004, Part 1, every name must consist of a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element; names may be in English or French (or a combined English and French form) and must use Roman script letters with no non-standard diacritical marks beyond the recognized French alphabet. The legal element for a ULC is 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' or 'SRI'. Numeric names are permitted under s 22(2)(c). The name must not be identical to, or too similar to, an existing BC or extra-provincial registered name or a reserved name, and must not be misleading as to the nature of the business. For the luxury-resale commerce business, descriptive tokens such as 'Vintage', 'Atelier', 'Collection' and 'Resale' are acceptable if distinctive elements are added; a bilingual name requires that both language versions be submitted for clearance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name approval may be extended once for an additional 56 days by filing an extension request via BC Corporate Online before expiry and paying the prescribed fee; extension is denied if the reservation has already expired, in which case a new name search and request must be filed. On rejection, the incorporator submits a Request for Reconsideration online within 30 days, accompanying a written legal memorandum, revised NUANS report, and any consent letters (e.g., letters from similarly named entity owners or the relevant financial regulator); the Registrar reconsiders under BCA s 22 and issues a final administrative determination. A further refusal may be challenged by judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241, within 60 days of the decision, or addressed pragmatically by filing amended Notice of Articles with a new approved name without payment of a second incorporation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially Permissible with Compliance Conditions: BCA s 25 requires a registered office located in BC at a physical address where service of process may be delivered; the registered records office under s 29 must be a physical location in BC open during business hours and capable of producing statutory records within required timeframes. A 'virtual office' is acceptable only where a staffing presence exists at a shared office or law-firm address in BC, mail is collected on site, service of process is accepted, and the records office is maintained at that address. Unstaffed virtual-mailbox addresses are non-compliant and will be rejected by the Registrar and by Canadian banks and escrow providers. For an online luxury-resale marketer, the registered office should coincide with the AML compliance address; separately, a meaningful commercial substance position (bank account, contracts, records, and operational decision-making) should be maintained in BC to preserve ULC independent substance for Canadian tax residence and US check-the-box pass-through treatment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (annual probability approximately 5%-10% for this e-commerce sector). Unannounced inspections are uncommon for non-FINTRAC-regulated provincial merchants; however, the Registrar may inspect records offices upon public complaint or regulatory enquiry, and Canada Revenue Agency or FINTRAC may conduct a premises visit during a suspected-money-laundering or unpaid-tax audit. Enhanced risk factors (UBO flagged as PEP, high-risk jurisdiction exposure, or repeated large-cash deposits) would elevate the likelihood to a Medium tier.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 19 (British Columbia), Part 2 (Incorporation), ss. 10–15 (incorporation documents and notice of articles), ss. 49–51 (directors and officers), ss. 142–146 (share subscription and issuance); BC General Regulation, BC Reg. 33/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Incorporation and Corporate Registry, BC Registry Services, Deputy Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Government of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Incorporation Application, together with optional Company Articles (Form 1A) and Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an unlimited liability company in BC. Shares may be authorized and issued for any lawful consideration; no escrow account or deposit requirement is imposed for ordinary private companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscribers of the unlimited liability company [Company Name] hereby subscribe for 100 common shares at a stated capital of $1.00 each, and the directors are authorized to issue the same upon acceptance. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office of the Company shall be established at [Registered Address], British Columbia, and the office shall be operated during statutory business hours. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the appointment of [Director Name] and [Officer Name] as directors and President/Secretary, respectively, is hereby ratified, and such officers are authorized to execute all banking, escrow, and commercial agreements for the Company. This resolution may be executed electronically and is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Reservation and Corporate Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – Name Reservation Online Portal, Government of British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the BC Corporate Online Registry, specifying the proposed unlimited liability company name, and, if required, attach a name search report from an approved corporate registry agent. Ensure the name ends with 'Unlimited Liability Company' or the applicable abbreviation 'ULC'.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged, the applicant may file a revised name reservation with an alternative list of available names within the statutory correction period and pay the relevant re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Incorporation Documents and Unlimited Liability Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator / Legal counsel / Authorized Corporate Services Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the necessary incorporation filings, namely the Notice of Articles and, where custom provisions are required, the Company Articles. For an unlimited liability company, the articles must clearly state that the liability of shareholders is unlimited. The formation instrument must set out the share structure, registered office address, first directors, and mailing address for the company.
required_dossiers: Custom Articles (Form 1A) if electing not to use standard articles
Consent to act as first director or officer
Registered office consent from the physical office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If documentation is incomplete, the registry will issue a requisition letter; the incorporator may amend and resubmit the electronic filing without incurring a penalty if done within the registry's stated response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Online Filing of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – BC Corporate Online (deputy registrar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to BC Corporate Online, complete the incorporation application for an unlimited liability company, attach the Notice of Articles and any opted-in custom articles, and electronically pay the required statutory filing fee. After processing, the registry will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and a BC Incorporation Number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected due to errors in the notice of articles, the applicant may correct the specified fields and resubmit through the online portal; fees prepaid for minor corrections are typically applied to the new filing within 7 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Profile Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services and Canada Revenue Agency (for Business Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance, login to the registry system to download the Certificate of Incorporation and effective Notice of Articles. Concurrently, request a Business Number from the Canada Revenue Agency using the issued incorporation number to allow for later GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income tax registration. Retain copies for bank onboarding and commercial counterparty verification.
required_dossiers: Notice of Articles with verified registration data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error, file a Form 'Correction Application' with the BC Registry; if the CRA account is not activated, call CRA's business services line and cite the incorporation number and certificate date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Resolutions and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Ltd. Liability Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution in lieu of meeting. The resolution must ratify share subscriptions, approve the registered office, appoint officers (President, Secretary, etc.), and authorize directors to open bank and escrow accounts. File any changes of director or address with the BC Registry if not already recorded in the Notice of Articles.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution or written consent
Consent and acceptance from each director and officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer refuses his or her appointment, convene a replacement resolution, file a Notice of Change of Directors within 15 days, and update the registry record accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Activation for Luxury Consignment E-Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize merchant onboarding with approved payment rails and escrow service providers. Obtain GST/HST registration, update the CRA business number profile with ISIC 4791/NAICS 459510 activity codes, and, if applicable, execute business agreements relating to consignment, authentication, and shipping. Arrange automatic inventory reconciliation for vintage luxury consignment sales.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is delayed, resubmit the BC incorporation certificate and provide explanatory cover letter; if a payment platform rejects onboarding, adjust the AML/KYC data package and resubmit the application to the platform's compliance review queue.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For all leased warehouse and office spaces, obtain municipal fire safety clearance and full compliance with WorkSafe BC occupational health and safety obligations. No special industrial civil-defense or structural-load certification is triggered for the mere warehousing and online resale of luxury goods.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – canada.ca; British Columbia Ministry of Finance (BC MF) for provincial PST
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST registration account. Submit articles of incorporation, registered office address, director information, and projected Canadian taxable supply revenue. Non-resident directors may require additional identity verification. File GST/HST returns electronically (NETFILE). For BC provincial sales tax (PST), register separately with the BC Ministry of Finance if selling goods or services subject to PST in British Columbia.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention Article IV(7), a Canadian ULC may elect to be treated as a corporation for U.S. federal tax purposes; absent such election, the ULC may be treated as a fiscally transparent/pass-through entity for U.S. purposes. For Canadian income tax, the ULC remains an entity-level taxpayer. GST/HST rules allow related-corporation elections under Section 156 of the Excise Tax Act to avoid tax on certain intercompany supplies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Canada during any preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; non-resident online platform operators may be required to register without the small-supplier threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. GST/HST returns and invoices are transmitted electronically using GST/HST NETFILE. E-invoicing is voluntary and interoperable through the Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 framework, but not yet statutory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada by a GST/HST registrant are zero-rated when title passes to a non-resident buyer and the goods are exported in a continuous unbroken flow of transport, or delivered outside Canada by the supplier or the non-resident purchaser. Certain offshore services performed for a non-resident are also zero-rated. For vintage luxury resale e-commerce, each sale must be supported by documentary proof of export to the non-resident customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Customs Export Declaration (CBSA GCA or approved commercial system)
Bill of Lading or waybill evidencing foreign destination
Commercial invoice, payment records, and inward remittance certificate or foreign bank statement when remittance scrutiny applies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may disallow the zero-rating, reassess uncollected GST/HST at the point of sale, and impose interest and penalties. Knowingly or fraudulently claiming zero-rating without required export proof triggers civil penalties up to 20% of the net tax amount, recovery for a 4-year reassessment window (extended indefinitely for misrepresentation), and potential criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) as the central monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the federal prudential supervisor of Schedule I and II banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the financial intelligence unit administering the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), cross-border currency and monetary instruments reporting, and money services business (MSB) registration and supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange-rate regime. Canada imposes no exchange-control restrictions on either current-account or capital-account transactions. Inbound equity and debt capital may be freely subscribed or lent into a British Columbia ULC; outbound profit remittance by dividend is unrestricted under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act (SBC 2002, c. 57), subject only to board solvency tests and non-resident Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reducible). For ISIC 4791 online luxury resale, the only compliance duties are reporting-based: FINTRAC EFT reports for wire transfers at or above C$10,000, large cash transaction reports at or above C$10,000, MSB registration for payment processors, and functional-currency tax reporting under Income Tax Act section 261 if the ULC books are kept in a foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rule applies in Canada. Exporters are not subject to any timeline for repatriation, any mandatory conversion ratio, or any export-proceeds certificate. The BC ULC may retain USD, EUR, or other foreign-currency proceeds indefinitely in a foreign-currency operating account maintained with a Canadian Schedule I bank, convert at commercial discretion, and settle non-resident supplier invoices without central-bank approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational Multi-Currency Business Account (CAD/USD)
Business Chequing Account; USD Operating Account
Operational Account; Foreign-Currency USD Account; Treasury Liquidity Sweep
International Trade Settlement Account; Operational Clearing Account
Operational Business Account; Escrow-Pay Sponsor Sub-Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium on a licensed-sponsored basis, and not viable as a standalone direct-settlement treasury rail. Canada has no statutory EMI category, and UK or EU EMI licences do not passport into British Columbia. An offshore digital EMI may lawfully act only as a technology and FX-liquidity wrapper, while all CAD-denominated clearing, settlement, merchant payouts, and payout reserves must route through a FINTRAC-registered Canadian MSB or a Schedule I bank sponsor, such as the Stripe Canada Ltd. MSB arrangement and Escrow_Pay's Canadian sponsor-bank structure. Direct treasury domiciliation solely in an offshore EMI settlement account is non-compliant for CAD inflows; the ULC must maintain a registered Canadian bank account as its treasury master account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video onboarding is legally permitted under the PCMLTFA when the bank applies a FINTRAC-compliant dual-verification process, but BC Schedule I banks commonly impose physical identity interviews for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced online resale ULC whose directors are non-resident or whose signatories are remote. To avoid underwriting delay, at least one director, authorized signatory, or a notarized resident power-of-attorney holder should attend an in-person branch interview in British Columbia and present a passport, proof of residential address, and the complete corporate KYC bundle. Residual enhanced due diligence may require an additional attestation from a Canadian CPA or notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement processor opacity: aggregated Stripe and Escrow_Pay marketplace flows obscure underlying counterparties and may be mischaracterized as unlicensed sub-account or shadow treasury activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed processor merchant agreements; FINTRAC MSB registration evidence for Stripe; monthly consolidated settlement files mapping transaction ID, consignor, SKU, and buyer jurisdiction; platform consignor onboarding and KYC policy; source-of-funds ledger; reserve and payout-hold rules; processor compliance maps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value used-luxury goods risk: designer handbags and timepieces attract typologies of theft, fencing, counterfeit laundering, and over-valuation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent authentication certificates (Entrupy, Authenticate First, Real Authentication); per-SKU graded condition and provenance records; acquisition invoices and consignment receipts; insurance valuation schedule; British Columbia Personal Property Security Act (PPSA) search showing no lien over inventory; documented chain of title from licensed dealers or auction vendors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX velocity and structuring red flags: frequent USD/CAD conversions plus aggregated EFTs near the C$10,000 FINTRAC threshold may trigger structuring alerts or incomplete source-of-funds attribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury dashboard reconciling every payment rail; daily FX and cash-flow forecast; bank-statement-matched reconciliation of gross remittances versus net payouts; signed Stage-4 treasury policy; CPA agreed-upon-procedures letter; system configuration prohibiting cash deposits and immaterial unlinked deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC structure opacity and unlimited-liability ambiguity: a pass-through-eligible ULC may be mistaken for a hybrid or disregarded entity, and banks demand clear beneficial-ownership identification and capital-sufficiency evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC registrar transparency-register extract identifying significant individuals; organizational chart reaching the ultimate natural-person UBO; notice of articles and Unlimited Liability Corporation certificate; ULC pass-through election documentation; board resolutions and signing authorities; shareholder register; section 232 corporate records retention confirmation at the BC registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and remote signatories: sanctions or PEP screening gaps and jurisdictional opacity in director home countries constitute a standard EDD blocker.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Liveness-verified passport copies for all directors and UBOs; OFAC/EU/UK/UN sanctions and PEP screening outputs; FINTRAC beneficial-ownership declaration; notarized resident signatory power of attorney; directors residential address verification; negative-news and registry-integrity reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound funding for the BC ULC is effected by equity subscription or by non-resident shareholder loan. Compliant routing requires a SWIFT MT103 wire with a standard purpose-of-payment narrative and ISO 20022 external purpose code EQUI for equity injection or INTC for intercompany loan; USD is cleared over Fedwire or CHIPS, CAD over Lynx; the beneficiary account is held in the ULC name at a BC branch of a Schedule I bank. Bank-side verification requires a share subscription agreement, board resolution, share certificates, an executed shareholder loan agreement with arm's-length interest, BC corporate register extracts, and a CPA flow-through-funds letter validating source of wealth. Investment Canada Act notification to Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada is triggered only where enterprise value exceeds the applicable threshold, currently C$5M or higher for WTO investors.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for ISIC 4791 luxury resale are cleared through five rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 bank wires for consignor payouts and high-value auction procurements, with OFAC/UN/EU sanctions pre-screening and FINTRAC EFT reporting when the wire is at or above C$10,000; (2) documentary commercial letters of credit, sight or usance, for EU and Asian wholesale suppliers; (3) Canadian domestic clearing through Lynx and Real-Time Rail for CAD obligations; (4) Stripe Connect and Escrow_Pay API payout rails for marketplace disbursements to consignors and settlements; (5) multi-currency batch payouts through a bank-sponsored treasury platform for non-CAD beneficiaries. All outbound transactions require KYC-complete beneficiary files and reconciliation to the underlying consignment or purchase order.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forward contracts with terms up to 24 months under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with a Schedule I bank; no Bank of Canada approval required.
Vanilla CAD/USD FX call and put options executed under the same ISDA/CSA credit documentation.
Cross-currency swaps exchanging CAD/USD notional principals and interest streams for hedging foreign-currency funding and balance-sheet exposure.
CME-listed CAD/USD futures (6C contract) and options for exchange-traded liquidity hedging of short-horizon FX exposure.
FX rolling forwards and non-deliverable forwards are not required because CAD is fully deliverable, but they are legally permissible in Canada if exotic non-CAD underlying exposure must be hedged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Corporate Annual Report (Annual Return to the Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies – BC Registries and Online Services, Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months of the incorporation anniversary, i.e., no later than the last day of the month following the anniversary month (BCBCA s. 273).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty CAD $45.75 as prescribed, in addition to the CAD $70 base filing fee; continued annual-report delinquency triggers a Registrar's strike-off notice and administrative dissolution under BCBCA s. 422 after the statutory notice period (approximately 60 days); a dissolved ULC loses capacity to carry on business and must be restored to resume operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal plus BC provincial corporate income tax; includes BC ULC treaty flow-through reconciliation for non-resident members)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), assessed jointly with the BC Ministry of Finance under the Tax Collection Agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's taxation year-end (ITA s. 150(1)); for a December 31 year-end, the return is due by June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months) under ITA s. 162(1); prescribed daily compounded interest; gross-negligence penalty up to 50% of understated income under ITA s. 163(2); CRA may issue statutory demands and register liens.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T106 Information Return – Transactions and Loans with Non-Resident Members (relevant to ULC pass-through equity, member current accounts, and cross-border payments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – International and Large Business Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the T2 return, no later than 6 months after the taxation year-end (ITA s. 162(7)).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD $100 per failure under ITA s. 162(7); additional CAD $25 per day for an unsatisfied CRA demand under ITA s. 162(8); knowing omissions attract gross-negligence penalties up to 50% of the related tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation – Transparency Register Update and Directors' Verification Resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Records Office (internal statutory records under BCBCA s. 119.1; no separate provincial UBO registry filing is currently required for BCBCA companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each fiscal year-end, and within 15 days after any share transfer or new member admission that changes significant control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers face offence liability – fines up to CAD $100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years for false statements or unlawful failures (BCBCA s. 427); inaccurate UBO records block corporate due diligence, financing, and annual-report certification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (or Unanimous Written Member Resolution Waiving the AGM) and Annual Statutory Register Audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members of the ULC (BCBCA s. 234); Corporate Records Office for the concurrent register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM, where not waived, must be held no later than 15 months after the previous AGM; register audit must be completed before the BC Annual Report filing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of director duties (BCBCA s. 136) may expose directors to personal liability; non-maintenance of statutory registers is an offence under the BCBCA general offence provisions (s. 427); register shortfalls also prevent reliable certification of the annual return and may trigger compliance orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return and Remittance (applicable where the corporation holds annual-filer status under the Excise Tax Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual GST/HST filers (ETA s. 238); interim monthly or quarterly reporting applies where taxable supplies exceed the prescribed threshold or where the CRA has revoked annual-filer status.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late remittance penalty of 6% plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months); prescribed daily interest; CRA may cancel annual-filer status, require monthly or quarterly filing, withhold refunds, and issue garnishments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: BCBCA imposes no revenue or asset threshold: every BC company must appoint an independent auditor at the annual meeting unless all members unanimously resolve to waive the audit requirement (BCBCA s. 221). For a pass-through ULC, the unanimous waiver is commonly exercised; audit remains compulsory where any member, lender, or treaty counterparty requires audited financial statements or where the unanimous waiver is revoked.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private BC corporations default to Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) per CPA Canada Handbook Part II; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are permitted. Financial statements must support the Canada–US treaty flow-through election and the CRA T2 reconciliation. Record retention follows the company's 7-year policy, exceeding the 6-year ITA s. 230 minimum while statutory registers are retained for the life of the company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually at fiscal year-end, the board passes a written resolution confirming every individual with significant control (beneficial owner or controller holding 25% or more of voting rights, economic interest, or de facto control, per BCBCA s. 119.1). The BC Transparency Register is updated within 15 days after any share transfer, share issuance, or change in control; signed member declarations are archived in the corporate minutes; the register must be produced to BC Registry or enforcement authorities upon demand. The federal CBCA beneficial-ownership registry does not apply to a BCBCA-incorporated ULC, and a BC public UBO registry filing is not yet operative.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Transparency Register of Individuals with Significant Control (BCBCA s. 119.1)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – 750 per year (CAD 350 – 1,000) for BC registered office and records office agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 8,000 per year (CAD 5,500 – 11,000); waived by unanimous member resolution where permitted under BCBCA s. 221
